messages:
mia: quick PSA — set up a cool-mist humidifier because my plants were dying. now my laptop wifi keeps dropping when the mist is on. anyone seen this before? photos attached 📸
akash: wait the mist is literally hitting your router or antenna? :sweat_smile:
mia: not directly, it's on the bookshelf beside the router (like 1.2m away) but the mist drifts over when the fan is on.
drew: moisture + electronics = questionable mix. might condense on antennas or corrode contacts over time.
flora: could be that the aerosolized water is changing dielectric properties near the antenna, causing attenuation. also sensors on some devices throttle when humidity changes.
mia: interesting. i did a quick wifi log: disconnects align with humidifier cycles.
netbot: [automated] On 2390011233 detected 12 brief DHCP renew retries from device "mia-mbp" within 7 minutes. Associated AP: "Mesh-Node-1" channel 6. No wide-area outage.
akash: try moving humidifier to the other side of the room, or raise the router a bit. also put a small tray underneath the humidifier to catch overspray.
drew: try lowering mist output first. if it's ultrasonic, the fine particulate can hang in the air longer. mechanical evaporative humidifiers produce less aerosol.
mia: poll: should i (1) move humidifier away, (2) put router in cupboard-high position, (3) get a different humidifier? vote 1️⃣ 2️⃣ 3️⃣
flora: 1️⃣ - simplest test
akash: 2️⃣ - raise router >1.8m if possible
drew: 3️⃣ - swap to evaporative if you want long-term solution
mia: updating: moved humidifier to kitchen counter and reduced mist to low. so far 0 disconnects for 20 minutes 
netbot: [info] Reminder: keep networking equipment away from direct moisture sources. See internal KB: http://tiny.cc/hw-care
flora: also, clean your router vents — mineral deposits from humidifiers can clog vents over time.
mia: noted. also will move the houseplants to window shelf so the humidifier isn't blowing across the electronics. will report back after a day of testing 🌱
akash: pro tip: silica gel packets in router enclosure? maybe overkill but good for long vacations.
drew: follow-up pic pls when you have new layout 4f7
mia: will do — and thanks for the quick fixes!
